 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents on account of death of Srirama S.N., who is husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioners No.2 to 4 and son of petitioners No.5 and 6, in a road traffic Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
2 accident.
2.

The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-05-2019 at about 12:00 p.m., at Tumkur- Bengaluru NH-48 service road,
Chikkabidarakallu, Opposite to Marison Factory, the respondent No.1 drove his motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JM-5011 Yamaha R-15 from Jindal to Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Hero Honda Passion Plus bearing No. KA-02-EW-6439 of the deceased Srirama S.N., from the backside to the vehicle.
Due to the said accident, the deceased fell down along with his motorcycle and sustained severe head injuries and injuries to other parts of the body.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Sapthagiri Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient and during the course of treatment he died in the hospital on 28-05-2019.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was running a provision store and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, the petitioners with a mala-fide intention have wrongfully implicated him and his vehicle.
He has contended that, his vehicle was not involved in any accident.
He has denied the age, avocation, income of the deceased and relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
He has admitted that, he is the owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JM-5011 and contended that, he was having valid and effective driving licence to drove the above said motorcycle.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has denied the existence of insurance policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.
KA-02-JM-5011 of the respondent No.1, as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident.

Further it is contended that, the deceased was not wearing helmet while driving the vehicle at the time of accident and there is one Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
3 day delay in lodging the complaint.

It has contended that, the deceased was negligently driving the vehicle in the middle of the road, without following the road rules and all of a sudden came in front of the vehicle of the respondent No.1 and contributed the accident.
The entire negligence is on the part of the deceased to the cause the accident.
It has further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the insurer of the vehicle bearing No.KA-02-EW-6439 is absolutely necessary party to the petition.
It has further contended that, the deceased was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
The respondent No.2 in its additional written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 i n r e s p e c t o f t h e v e h i c l e b e a r i n g N o .
K A - 0 2 - J M - 5 0 1 1 a n d t h e p o l i c y b e a r i n g No.3006/171000985/00/B00, which is valid from midnight of 16-05-2019 to midnight of 15-05-2020.
The accident had taken place on 13-05-2019 and as on the date of accident there is no coverage of the policy.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Sri Srirama S.N., succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 13-05-2019 at about 12.00 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MJ-5011 ?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
7. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 and closed their side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its offical as R.W.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R.1.

The respondent No.1 has got examined himself as R.W.2 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.2 to 4.
8.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
4 10.
Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 13-05-2019 at about 12:00 p.m., at Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 service road, Chikkabidarakallu, Opposite to Marison Factory, the respondent No.1 drove his motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JM-5011 Yamaha R-15 from Jindal to Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Hero Honda Passion Plus bearing No. KA-02-EW-6439 of the deceased Srirama S.N., from the backside to the vehicle.
Due to the said accident, the deceased fell down along with his motorcycle and sustained severe head injuries and injuries to other parts of the body.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Sapthagiri Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient and during the course of treatment he died in the hospital on 28-05-2019.
Further they have contended that, before accident the deceased was running a provision store and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
11. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, she has got marked total 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of atopsy report, Ex.P.8 is death certificate, Ex.P.9 are hospital and lab bills (total 60), Ex.P.10 are medical bills (total 90),

Ex.P.11 is notarised copy of driving licence, Ex.P.12 is notarised copy of R.C., Ex.P.13 is notarised copy of ID card and Ex.P14 are pay slips (total 2).
12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, on 13-05-2019 at about 12:00 p.m., at Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 service road,
Chikkabidarakallu, Opposite to Marison Factory, the respondent No.1 drove his motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JM-5011 Yamaha R-15 from Jindal to Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Hero Honda Passion Plus bearing No. KA-02-EW-6439 of the deceased Srirama S.N.,
from the backside to the vehicle.
Due to the said accident, the deceased fell down along with his motorcycle and sustained severe head injuries and injuries to other parts of the body.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Sapthagiri Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient and during the course of treatment he died in the hospital on 28-05-2019.
The oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence marked as Ex.P.1 to 14.

Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross- examined P.W.1 in length,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

On the other hand, except the self serving statements of the respondent No.1 & 2, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence adduced by the respondents to rebut the final report of the investigation officer and other police documents produced by the petitioners, with regard to cause of the accident is due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1.
13.

Further, though, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above facts in their written statements, they have not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.

It is pertinent to note that, the P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 in her cross- examination Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
5

that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of her deceased husband,
who was the rider of the Hero-Honda motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-EW-6439 and not due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 02-JM-5011 i.e.
respondent No.1.

Learned counsel for respondent No.1 vehemently argued that, the Ex.P.5 spot sketch clearly speaks that, the motorcycle of respondent No.1 bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JM-5011 was front side and the motorcycle of the deceased bearing Reg. No. KA-02-EW-6439 was back side.
The same is admitted by P.W.1 in her cross- examination.

Therefore, it clearly goes to show that, the alleged accident has caused due to self rash and negligent driving of the deceased and dashing his motorcycle to the ongoing motorcycle of the respondent No.1 from behind.

The above arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 are not acceptable, as the sketch of the scene of offence or spot of accident is prepared by the investigation officer after the alleged accident had taken place and the position of vehicles involved in the accident are shown as per the situation at the time of preparing sketch.

It is known fact that, due to force impact of dashing of two vehicles,
especially two wheeler vehicles, in a very high speed, either from the front side or from backside, one cannot guess where the said vehicles go and hault.

Mere on the basis of position of the vehicles involved in the accident shown in the sketch prepared by the investigation officer while drawing spot mahazer, which is prepared after the occurrence of accident, it is not possible to come to the conclusion with regard to what was the exact position of said vehicles before the accident and due to whose negligence the said accident has caused, unless it is corroborated with the evidence of eye-witness to the said accident.

14. The Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 spot sketch, clearly speaks that, the accident has taken place on extreme left side of 22 feet width service-road beside Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 National Highway road.
Further it reveals that, there was sufficient space towards the right side of the place of accident to avoid accident.

If really as contended by the respondents, the rider of offending vehicle bearing No. KA- 02-JM-5011 i.e. respondent No.1 was not riding his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner, definitely he would have avoided the said accident.

Further it is pertinent to note,
as per Ex.P.6 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident had not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not occurred due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of deceased,
then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.3, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JM-5011.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence led by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing worth has been elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased and there is no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JM-5011.
15.

Further, the Ex.P.7 atopsy report/Post-motem report, clearly speaks that, deceased Srirama S.N.,
has died due to respiratory failure as a result of adult acute respiratory syndrome developed consequent upon multiple injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident,
Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
6 involvement of the offending vehicle and the cause of death of deceased Srirama, in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
18.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Sriram S.N., has succumbed to the injuries sustained in motor vehicle accident occurred on 13-05-2019 at about 12.00 p.m., on Tumkur-Bengaluru NH- 48 service road, Chikkabidarakallu, Opposite to Marison Factory, due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JM-5011.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that,
the alleged accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending motorcycle, bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JM-5011 and due to said impact, the deceased Srirama S.N.,
sustained grievous injuries on his head and was succumbed to said injuries in the hospital.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, the petitioners have produced the xerox copy of their Aadhar cards.

The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the daughters,
petitioner No.4 is the son, petitioner NO.5 is the father and petitioner No.6 is the mother of deceased Srirama S.N.
The petitioners have not tendered and got marked the said documents in their evidence, for the reason best known to them.

But, it is pertinent to note that, nowhere in their written statements or in the cross- examination of P.W.1, the respondents have specifically denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Srirama S.N.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to rely on the said documents and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Srirama S.N.
20.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, " The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
7
pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
10. The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.

According to Section 2(11) CPC, "legal representative" means a person who in law represents the Tractor and Trally bearing No.AP-03-AN-8690 & AP-03-AN-8712 estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued.
Almost in similar terms is the definition of legal representative under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 i.e. under Section 2(1)(g).

As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.

entities.text: Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative".

As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a wife, husband, parent and child.

entities.text: Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Manjuri Bera (supra), in paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act, the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation.
In the concurring judgment of Justice S. H. Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased.
As a result, the legal representative of the deceased would inherit the estate.
Indeed, in that case, the Court was dealing with the case of a married daughter of the deceased and the efficacy of Section 140 of the Act.
Nevertheless, the principle underlying the exposition in this decision would clearly (claimants) even though they are major sons of the deceased and also earning.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
8 21.

According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
22. The compensation towards loss of dependency: The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are the children and petitioners No.5 and 6 are the parents of the deceased Srirama S.N.
The petitioners have established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased.
Further, they have stated that, they were depending upon the deceased.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased : The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 45 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.11 driving licence of deceased Srirama S.N., wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 27-05-1974.
Admittedly, the accident has taken place on 13-05-2019 at 12:00 P.M.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 45 years.
The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was doing provision store business and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
In this regard, they have produced Ex.P.13 notarised copy of ID card and Ex.P.14 pay slips (total).
But, they have not examined the author of the said documents in order to prove the contents of said documents.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as income of the deceased as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."

entities.text: G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2019.

Therefore, the notional income of the deceased as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be treated as Rs.
14,000/- per month.
Therefore, the annual income of the deceased in the present case is held as Rs.1,68,000/-.

ii) As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are also entitled for future prospects of the deceased, though he was not a permanent employee as on the date of death.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was aged about 45 years and was not a permanent employee, the future prospects would be 25% of his income, which comes to Rs.42,000/-.
Therefore, the future prospects of the deceased is held as Rs.42,000/-.

If this income is added to the notional income,
then it comes to Rs.2,10,000/-.
Further, the annual income of the deceased comes within the Nagarathnamma vs Mahadeva.C.B on 7 October, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33698512/
9 exemption limits as per Income Tax Act.
iii) The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier:
The family of the deceased consist of 6 persons i.e., petitioners No.1 to 6.
The total number of dependents of the deceased are 6.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 1/4th of the total income, which comes to Rs.52,500/-.
After deducting 1/4th out of total income, towards the personal expenses of deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.1,57,500/-.
iv) As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 45 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 14.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is held as Rs. 1,57,500 x 14 = Rs.22,05,000/-.
v) Compensation under conventional heads:
In the present case, admittedly, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are the children and petitioners No.5 and 6 are the parents of deceased Srirama S.N..
Hence, the petitioner No.1 to 6 are entitled for compensation under the head of spousal, parental and filial consortium.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
 a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-
 b) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/-
 c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation under above heads has to be enhanced 10% for every 3 years.
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.

Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of spousal,
parental and filial consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioner No.1 to 6 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.
vi) Medical expenses:
The petitioners have deposed that, they have incurred huge amount towards medical, treatment, conveyance, nourishment, attendant charges and traveling expenses etc.
In order to prove the same, they have produced 150 hospital bills, lab bills and medical bills, as per Ex.P.9 and 10.
